Senses.Explanation: To deceive one another is a recurring accusation or warning in Chan address. Faxiu Yuantong, Baichi Xingyuan, and Hongzhi Zhengjue use it when a proposed understanding, an apparently obvious scene, or even lantern and pillar would collude in passing off an answer that has not been seen through. One hall address asks listeners not to blame Faxiu Yuantong for deceiving them if they cannot identify the color of wind. Baichi Xingyuan goes further: even lantern and exposed pillar ‘deceive one another,’ making reciprocal collusion part of the image. Hongzhi Zhengjue uses the negated assurance inside a compact assurance, while Dahui and Yunwai warn against mutual deception. The polarity changes—accusation, warning, or denial—but the reciprocal relation remains one thing.
